sentences.text:
This application has been filed under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for regular bail in connection with FIR being C.R. No.11208055210235 of 2021 registered with D.C.B. Police Station, Rajkot City for offences punishable under sections 465, 467, 471, 272, 274, 275, 34 and 120B of IPC.
2.

Mr. Manan K.Paneri, learned advocate for the applicant submitted that the allegation against the present applicant is of selling the Ayurvedic medicines of expiry date and further allegations are of using false documents in the form of sticker pasted on the Ayurvedic medicines with FSSAI number of the complainant.

Mr. Paneri submitted that the F.I.R. does not invoke the provisions of Drugs and Cosmetic Act and there is no direct evidence to show that applicant was selling the R/CR.MA/19455/2021 ORDER DATED: 06/01/2022 expired Ayurvedic tablets.
Mr. Paneri stated that the statements of the witnesses in the charge-sheet shows that it was legal purchase of the medicines and the applicant is selling the Ayurvedic medicines.

He submits that as per the government guidelines, there is no requirement of any licence and the applicant being the Paresh Haribhai Chovatiya (Doctor) vs State Of Gujarat on 6 January, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153559490/
1 businessman, employing Ayurvedic Doctors and is regularly paying the G.S.T. on the sale and also pays income tax.

sentences.text: He states that it may appear that the Ayurvedic medicines have lost their shelf-life and that would be the question of fact, be decided during the trial in absence of any provisions under the Drugs and Cosmetic Act applying in the present matter.
Mr. Paneri stated that applicant cannot be dragged under the provisions of IPC.
It was, therefore, prayed that the present application may be allowed and the applicant herein may be released on regular bail.

3. Mr. J.K. Shah, learned Additional Public Prosecutor, referring to the documents on record stated that, when the premises of the applicant was raided and search was made, lot of stickers were seized of different manufacturers and the said machine was also found.
He submits that various tablets with the affixed stickers worth Rs.1,34,000/- were also recovered; no documents have been produced by the applicant to show the legal purchase.
It was, therefore, prayed that no discretion may be exercised in favour of the applicant.
Heard learned advocates on both the sides and perused the material on record.

Taking the fact into consideration that the goods which was seized were considered as Ayurvedic medicines and further the fact that no proceedings have been made against the applicant alleging that he is selling fake or sub-standard medicines.
The statements of witnesses suggest the legal purchase of the medicines; however, whether the medicines could be considered of expiry date or having lost the shelf value, is a matter of evidence.
Thus, taking into consideration the punishment prescribed and the nature of allegation, this Court finds this to be a fit case where discretion could be exercised in favour of the applicant.
5. Hence, the present application is allowed.
